newsitem.title: BELGIUM: The Commissioner, her mother and the EU currency.
newsitem.headline: The Commissioner, her mother and the EU currency.

text.p: European Commissioner Emma Bonino has faced the wrath of fishermen from Britain to Canada and braved the conditions of refugee camps in eastern Zaire.
But the thing she really fears is the switch to a single European currency.

"The lira may not exactly be the best currency in the world, but when I want to know whether something is expensive or not I calculate in lira, even if I'm paid in Belgian francs," the Italian commissioner said on Friday.

Bonino, who shares responsibility for ensuring the people of the European Union get used to the idea of paying for everything in Euros, as the currency will be called, said the problem would be even worse for her 77-year-old mother.

She, and millions of other people in the Union, had never learned to convert their money into a foreign currency, she told a conference on the changeover to the single currency organised by the European Mortgage Federation.

EU countries that qualify for monetary union will see their currencies irrevocably locked into the single currency on January 1, 1999, although it will be another three years before Euro notes and coins get into people's pockets.
